purpose: Assess candidate improvements to probability estimation using existing forecasts, without fitting or selecting a new model.
verification: Probability scores independently recomputed from identical 161 saved earlier-outcome forecasts. Historical stake alternatives recomputed from each saved model forecast and the same side-specific costs.
interpretation: The market quote benchmark has the best point-estimate score among these models; saved paired uncertainty intervals do not establish superiority. The simpler market-offset confidence model still produces a large second stake. These results motivate testing market-centered shrinkage, not claiming it already improves forecasts.
proposed_estimator: A market-offset confidence calibration with confidence adjustments shrunk toward zero; compare with the market-only baseline using earlier-data-only tuning and subsequent forecasts. Hierarchical confidence deviations are a secondary candidate if the common effect proves inadequate.
not_established: No optimal shrinkage amount or hierarchical prior scale has been estimated here.
No new win probability is assigned to either historical fight.
A narrower historical drawdown is not evidence of more accurate probabilities.
Posterior uncertainty alone does not automatically reduce single-bet expected-log-optimal sizing at a fixed posterior mean.
